title: Friction (static/kinetic, inclines, stacked blocks)
theory: Static friction adjusts itself up to $f_s \le \mu_s N$; sliding starts when demand exceeds supply. Kinetic friction is fixed at $f_k = \mu_k N$ and points opposite the **relative** sliding of the two surfaces — not necessarily opposite the body's motion. On an incline, $N = mg\cos\theta$ and the slide condition is $\tan\theta > \mu$. In stacked blocks the friction from below is the **only** horizontal force on the top block, so it *accelerates* it forward; its N3 reaction decelerates the lower block. The pair vanishes the instant the velocities match.

formulas.description: heat generated = friction force × relative sliding distance

framework: Static or kinetic (is there relative sliding *now*)?
Direction of $f_k$: opposite this surface's motion relative to the other.
Find when sliding stops (equal velocities) and switch regimes.

parts.parameters:
- Given: box of mass $m$ on incline angle $\theta$; static coefficient $\mu$.
- Find: condition for the box to slide.
parts.formulas: driving force $mg\sin\theta$ vs. max static friction $\mu mg\cos\theta$.
parts.conclusion: $m$ and $g$ cancel — pure geometry. The critical angle ($\tan\theta_c = \mu$) is the "angle of repose"; memorize the equivalence both ways.

parts.title: Force acting on Q
parts.parameters:
- Given: plank P (mass $M$) on a smooth floor; block Q (mass $m$) on top; both at rest; at $t=0$ P receives speed $v_0$ (rightward $= +$); kinetic coefficient $\mu$ between P and Q; velocities become equal at $t = T$.
- Find: forces on Q and on P; $v_P(t)$; $T$; relative sliding distance.
- Diagram: Q rides on P; for $0<t<T$, P moves right faster than Q, so P's surface slides rightward **relative to Q**.
parts.formulas: $f_k = \mu N$, $N = mg$; direction = direction the surface under Q moves relative to Q $= +$.
parts.conclusion: friction is the only horizontal force on Q and it pushes Q **forward**. "Friction opposes motion" is wrong as stated — it opposes *relative* motion.

parts.title: Force acting on P
parts.parameters:
- Given: plank P (mass $M$) on a smooth floor; block Q (mass $m$) on top; both at rest; at $t=0$ P receives speed $v_0$ (rightward $= +$); kinetic coefficient $\mu$ between P and Q; velocities become equal at $t = T$.
- Find: forces on Q and on P; $v_P(t)$; $T$; relative sliding distance.
- Diagram: Q rides on P; for $0<t<T$, P moves right faster than Q, so P's surface slides rightward **relative to Q**.
parts.formulas: Newton's third law; smooth floor ⇒ nothing else horizontal.
parts.conclusion: a textbook action–reaction pair. Note it is $\mu mg$, **not** $\mu Mg$ — the normal force in this pair comes from Q's weight only.

parts.title: Velocity of P at time t
parts.parameters:
- Given: plank P (mass $M$) on a smooth floor; block Q (mass $m$) on top; both at rest; at $t=0$ P receives speed $v_0$ (rightward $= +$); kinetic coefficient $\mu$ between P and Q; velocities become equal at $t = T$.
- Find: forces on Q and on P; $v_P(t)$; $T$; relative sliding distance.
- Diagram: Q rides on P; for $0<t<T$, P moves right faster than Q, so P's surface slides rightward **relative to Q**.
parts.conclusion: deceleration scales with $m/M$. Meanwhile Q obeys $v_Q = \mu g t$ — independent of any mass.

parts.title: Time T when the velocities coincide
parts.parameters:
- Given: plank P (mass $M$) on a smooth floor; block Q (mass $m$) on top; both at rest; at $t=0$ P receives speed $v_0$ (rightward $= +$); kinetic coefficient $\mu$ between P and Q; velocities become equal at $t = T$.
- Find: forces on Q and on P; $v_P(t)$; $T$; relative sliding distance.
- Diagram: Q rides on P; for $0<t<T$, P moves right faster than Q, so P's surface slides rightward **relative to Q**.
parts.calculations: $v_0 - \frac{m}{M}\mu gT = \mu gT \Rightarrow v_0 = \mu g T\,\frac{M+m}{M} \Rightarrow T = \frac{M}{M+m}\cdot\frac{v_0}{\mu g}$.
parts.conclusion: faster route — momentum conservation (frictionless floor): $v_f = \frac{Mv_0}{M+m}$, then $T = v_f/(\mu g)$. Same result, half the algebra. Always keep two routes.

parts.title: Distance Q slides against P (0 → T)
parts.parameters:
- Given: plank P (mass $M$) on a smooth floor; block Q (mass $m$) on top; both at rest; at $t=0$ P receives speed $v_0$ (rightward $= +$); kinetic coefficient $\mu$ between P and Q; velocities become equal at $t = T$.
- Find: forces on Q and on P; $v_P(t)$; $T$; relative sliding distance.
- Diagram: Q rides on P; for $0<t<T$, P moves right faster than Q, so P's surface slides rightward **relative to Q**.
parts.formulas: relative speed $v_{rel}(t) = v_P - v_Q = v_0\!\left(1 - \frac{t}{T}\right)$ falls linearly ⇒ relative displacement = triangle area $\frac{1}{2}v_0T$.
parts.conclusion: energy audit: KE lost $= \frac{1}{2}Mv_0^2 - \frac{1}{2}(M+m)v_f^2 = \frac{Mm\,v_0^2}{2(M+m)}$; dividing by $\mu mg$ returns the same $d$ ✓. "Heat = friction × relative slide" is a recurring MEXT identity — own it.
